idiom_name: plain hub object holding a listener collection (stdlib Observable mixin for pure fan-out)
implementation_notes: Ruby needs no framework for Mediator: the hub is a plain object with an array or Set of listeners and methods like on/notify, and colleagues are duck-typed objects that register a block, a proc or an object responding to a method name. The stdlib Observable mixin is the library-grade fan-out half: including it provides add_observer/delete_observer and notify_observers, which calls each observer's update (or a named method) only after changed is asserted, and it also accepts procs via add_observer(proc, :call). Use Observable when the need is exactly broadcast; keep a hand-written hub when the mediator must route differently per event or return values, because Observable is notification, not coordination.
pitfalls: Blocks and procs registered on a long-lived hub keep their closures alive, so remove the listener when the colleague's lifecycle ends or the hub pins it forever.
notify runs synchronously on the calling thread and Ruby's GVL serialises handlers: a blocking listener stalls the hub, and an exception propagates to the caller unless rescued.
Observable requires changed to be set before notify_observers, so a missed changed call makes notifications vanish silently, and its peer hash holds observers strongly.
Mutating the listener array while notify iterates it skips or repeats handlers; iterate a dup when handlers may unsubscribe.
